correctness.rationale: The finite metric is admissible on 1<=t<=2, with the changed pair distance at most two through any other point. In anchored molecule coordinates, equilateral transportation balls decompose by signs into two simplices in each orthant; Vandermonde gives vol P_{d,1}=choose(2d,d)/d!. Removing the marked edge leaves two opposite exposed facets, because every integer tight spanning-tree Lipschitz potential has |f_a-f_b|<=2 and equality only at the positive/negative distinguished potential. Each exposed facet is a determinant-one (d-1)-crosspolytope, and moving the two molecule apices from +/-v to +/-v/t changes total volume by 2^d(1-1/t)/d!. For the polar, fix core-vertex potentials with range R; the endpoints share an interval of length 2-R, restricted to |f_a-f_b|<=t, yielding area (2-R)^2-((2-R)-t)_+^2; integrate using the exact range distribution of d-1 anchored core values to get d+1+(2/d)(1-(2-t)^d). Differentiating gives F_d(t) with derivative strictly negative on [1,2) for d>=3, and opposite endpoint signs, hence a unique maximum. At d=2 the product is (t+2)(4-t) and decreases beyond 1. C(2d,d)~4^d/sqrt(pi d) gives (2-t_d)^(d-1)=Theta(d^(3/2)2^(-d)), so t_d->3/2 and the relative gain is 1+2/[d(d+1)]+o(d^-2). Independently verified exact planar identity and strict derivative grid in d=3..30 (rational arithmetic), plus stationary tests, not an exhaustive proof.
residual_risks: The two-facet combinatorial classification uses that all other distances equal one; no extension to multiple defect edges is proved.
The family maximum is not a global optimum over all metrics; the gain is small for high d but mathematically exact.

value.rationale: The Mahler product is an affine-invariant quantity naturally associated with Lipschitz-free Banach balls, and a single variable metric-edge deformation isolates geometric transition mechanisms not visible in combinatorial counts. Exact primal and polar volume formulas, the change from boundary optimum at d=2 to unique interior optimum for every d>=3, and a universal t_d->3/2 limit give a complete motivated continuous extremal classification. The asymptotic gain of order d^-2 is small but the structural optimizer and phase change are substantive and not merely a tiny numerical improvement.
residual_risks: Constrained one-edge extremality does not settle all-metric Mahler optimization.
